civilization_label_resolution.label: Kyrgyz Civilization
civilization_label_resolution.reason: TheColdHands' Civilization VI mod explicitly uses 'Kyrgyz Civilization' as its game civilization and Manas as its leader. This is not by itself evidence for a historical polity of that exact identity.

narrative_activity.notes: UNESCO treats Manas as the central hero of the Kyrgyz oral epic tradition, whose trilogy narrates the unification of scattered tribes into one nation. A peer-reviewed study of epic historicism states that, in the epic storyline, Manas is elected khan, but proposes only a possible early-ninth-century historical prototype rather than an established identification. Scholarship on the epic's formation treats its chronology and historicism as debated and layered across long periods. ATLAS therefore records Manas as a legendary Person decision, not as a verified historical khan with an invented reign interval.

authoring_contract_blocker.problem: Current Human Authoring requires integer start and end historical years for every Activity.
authoring_contract_blocker.model_invariant: Unknown historical boundaries must not be replaced with fake years merely to satisfy transitional runtime constraints.
authoring_contract_blocker.required_resolution: Support Person creation and/or unresolved Activity authoring without fabricated temporal endpoints before compiling Manas into Production.

sources.title: Kyrgyz epic trilogy: Manas, Semetey, Seytek — UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage
sources.use: Establishes Manas as the central figure of a Kyrgyz oral epic tradition and the narrative theme of unifying scattered tribes.

sources.title: Kyrgyz-Chinese Ties in the Tang Era and Their Reflection in the Epic of Manas — Izvestiya of Altai State University
sources.use: States that in the epic storyline Manas is elected khan; the proposed early-ninth-century prototype is explicitly a scholarly hypothesis, not a secure historical identification.

sources.title: From Folk Epics to Epic Monuments: Studying and Publishing Epic Lore in the Soviet Union (1920s–1960s) — Journal of Central Asian History
sources.use: Documents scholarly debate over layers of the epic and notes that portrayals of Manas as khan were interpreted by Auezov as later transformations of an older clan-leader stratum.

sources.title: TheColdHands' Kyrgyz — Steam Workshop
sources.use: Confirms the user-supplied game context: Civilization 'Kyrgyz Civilization', Leader 'Manas'.
